key_insight: This paper shows that Real-Bogus classifiers for time-domain astronomy can be trained without human labels by using injected transients and mostly bogus survey data, while still staying robust to heavy label contamination. It also adds uncertainty quantification so the model can know when it is unsure.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of building reliable Real-Bogus classifiers when human-labeled data is expensive, sparse, noisy, or survey-dependent. It targets the need for a label-free training strategy that remains accurate under contaminated training sets and provides calibrated confidence estimates.
method: Train a deep learning Real-Bogus classifier using injected transient examples plus bogus-dominated survey data instead of manual labels.
Design the framework to be robust against strong class contamination, reducing sensitivity to noisy or imperfect training labels.
Include uncertainty quantification so predictions are accompanied by calibrated confidence estimates for downstream decision-making.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical template for learning from weak, noisy, or label-free data in high-volume scientific pipelines. The uncertainty-aware design makes the model more trustworthy for automated discovery systems where false positives and missed detections are costly.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing injected transients, bogus survey data, training, and Real-Bogus output
Comparison chart of performance under clean vs. contaminated labels
Uncertainty gauge or confidence bar attached to each prediction
Icon set illustrating real transient, bogus artifact, and uncertain sample
paper_title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
paper_authors: Raphaël Bonnet-Guerrini, Bruno Sanchez, Dominique Fouchez, Benjamin Racine, Maya Guy
